PHOTO: Anna Fratto | The South Pasadenan News | SPUSD

Beyond the numbers of a new district budget, the upcoming school board meeting touches the very heart of our community. From funding vital student resources to passing critical new student safety guidelines, local families have a lot riding on Tuesday night’s decisions.

As local students settle into the quiet rhythms of summer break, the vital machinery of our city’s public education system continues to hum. District administrators and elected board members are gearing up for one of the most consequential nights of the academic planning year.

On Tuesday, June 16, 2026, the South Pasadena Unified School District Board of Education will convene to shape the financial and operational future of our local schools. The open session begins at 6:30 p.m. at the District Office boardroom, located at 1100 El Centro Street in South Pasadena.

Funding the Students’ Future

At the core of Tuesday’s agenda is the formal adoption of the 2026-2027 District Budget. Assistant Superintendent of Business Services Dave Lubs will present the financial roadmap for the upcoming year. This budget dictates everything from campus maintenance to vital classroom resources.

Hand in hand with the budget is the approval of the Local Control and Accountability Plan. This comprehensive three-year strategy is designed to elevate student outcomes across the board. It specifically ensures equitable resources for English learners and low-income students in our community.

Student well-being takes center stage with a pivotal vote on Board Policy 4119.24, a measure governing adult and student interactions. This policy brings the district into compliance with California Senate Bill 848, a comprehensive child safety law.

The new state mandate significantly broadens misconduct disclosure requirements and safety planning across all public schools. For local parents, this represents a crucial step in maintaining transparency and securing the physical and emotional safety of children on campus.

Upgrading Facilities and Supporting Athletes

The consent agenda reveals a flurry of hyper-local improvements and community support measures. Students at Arroyo Vista Elementary will soon see campus upgrades, with a $48,925 contract slated for new site work and turf installation.

Meanwhile, our South Pasadena High School athletes are gearing up for another competitive season. The board is set to approve an overnight training camp in Big Bear for 30 varsity cross country runners. Head Coach Mike Parkinson, alongside his dedicated coaching staff and parent volunteers, will guide the students through their annual summer conditioning this August.

Ensuring every student receives the support they need remains a visible priority for the district. The board will review multiple service agreements with specialized local providers.

These partnerships include critical occupational, physical, and speech therapies for our special education students. By renewing contracts with facilities like the Center for Developing Kids and The Almansor Center, the district guarantees continuous, tailored care for its most vulnerable learners.

Make your Voice Heard

Civic engagement is the lifeblood of our local school system. Residents are encouraged to attend and lend their voices to the decision-making process.

When: Tuesday, June 16, 2026. Closed session begins at 5:30 p.m., and the public open session starts promptly at 6:30 p.m.

Where: SPUSD District Office, 1100 El Centro Street, South Pasadena, CA 91030.

Public Comment: Speaker cards must be submitted to the Secretary to the Superintendent prior to the beginning of the meeting. Speakers are allotted three minutes each.

Accommodations: To request disability-related modifications, contact Sylvia Carroll at the Office of the Superintendent (626-441-5810, ext. 1100, or [email protected]) at least 72 hours before the meeting.
